stem: A parcel-tracking company's engineering team wants its billing service to react immediately whenever a shipment's status changes in DynamoDB, without the billing service repeatedly asking the tracking table whether anything changed.

choices.text: Publish a status-change event and use an EventBridge rule to route matching events to the billing service
Create an EventBridge Scheduler schedule that invokes the billing service on a fixed one-minute rate
Have the billing service call GetItem against the tracking table before every billing transaction to check the current status
Enable DynamoDB Streams on the tracking table and have the billing service call GetRecords against the stream on a fixed interval

rationale: Publishing a status-change event and routing it with an EventBridge rule is an event-driven design: the billing service reacts the moment a matching event arrives, with no polling and no knowledge of the tracking table's internals. An EventBridge Scheduler schedule invokes its target at a fixed rate regardless of whether a status actually changed, so it is still time-driven rather than reacting to the real change, and it adds up to a minute of delay after a change happens. Having the billing service call GetItem before every transaction couples it tightly and synchronously to the tracking table instead of reacting to a decoupled event. Enabling DynamoDB Streams captures the change data, but calling GetRecords on a fixed interval still means the billing service is repeatedly asking whether anything new arrived, rather than being invoked automatically when a record does.
